propositions: The test uses a wall-clock timer to delete a planted index.lock, but on slow runners the timer fires while git commit holds its own real index.lock, causing git commit to fail with 'fatal: unable to write new index file'.

The test plants a young index.lock, calls git add/commit with force_reclaim=True (which removes the planted lock on first retry), then git commit creates its own real index.lock before the test's timer fires at t=0.4.
The timer body has no identity check and cannot distinguish between the test's planted lock and git's legitimate lock, so it indiscriminately deletes whichever exists at t=0.4.
On slow macOS py3.13 CI runners, git commit is still holding its lock when the timer fires (t≈0.4), whereas fast Linux runners complete git commit before the timer, masking the race.

The fix replaces the wall-clock threading.Timer with gitutil._retry_probe (a deterministic probe that fires after each retry attempt), allowing the test to release the planted lock only after observing the first failure, eliminating the race.
